voyage.name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
voyage.price: €12 full, €6 concessions; combined with Knossos (valid for 3 days) €20
voyage.content: Houses the most important and representative finds from Minoan civilisation and excavations across the island of Crete. Highlights include statues of the Snake Goddess, the Bull-Leaping Fresco, the Phaistos Disk, and Minoan seals and jewellery. Also includes a number of finds from Classical Greek and Roman periods.

voyage.name: Palace of Knossos
voyage.content: If you see just one ruin on Crete, see Knossos (in Greek it’s Κνωσός, stress is on the second syllable). The site is fairly compact, and much of it is accessible with restricted mobility. But 30 minutes will do it. It is one of six Minoan Palatial Centres to be listed as a world heritage site.

voyage.name: Koules
voyage.hours: Daily 08:00-20:00, limited hours during off season
voyage.content: Koules (Greek: Κούλες) was built by the Venetians in the 16th C. From the parapet, enjoy the view towards Dia Islet, where Jacques Cousteau found many sunken remains of Cretan sea trade.

voyage.name: Fortifications of Heraklion
voyage.content: The Fortifications of Heraklion are among the most impressive Venetian defensive works in the Mediterranean, encircling the old city of Heraklion. Built between the 15th and 17th centuries, their massive walls and bastions helped the city withstand a 21-year Ottoman siege—the longest in history—before falling in 1669. voyage.name: Historical Museum of Crete
voyage.price: €7.50 full, €4.50 concession, children 12 and under: free
voyage.hours: summer (Apr–Oct) Mon,Wed–Fr 10:00-17:00, Sat-Sun 11:00-17:00; winter (Nov–Mar) Mon–Fr 09:00-15:30, Sat-Sun 10:00-16:00
voyage.content: Covers the story of Crete from the Byzantine era to the present day. It includes material on World War II and the German occupation, which was displayed in the “Museum of the Battle for Crete and National Resistance” until it closed.

voyage.name: Loggia
voyage.content: An elegant city meeting place, built in 1628.

voyage.name: Natural History Museum of Crete
voyage.content: The Natural History Museum of Crete shows the natural environment of the Eastern Mediterranean area with a special emphasis on Greece and Crete.

voyage.name: Nikos Kazantzakis Museum
voyage.content: This museum in the village of Myrtia (Varvari), 20 km south of Heraklion, focuses on Crete's most prominent modern intellectual figure.

voyage.name: CretAquarium Thalassokosmos
voyage.content: The biggest aquarium in the Eastern Mediterranean.

voyage.name: Lychnostatis Open-Air Museum
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: Sun-Fri 09:00-14:00, closed Sat, closed Nov-Mar
voyage.content: Open-air Cretan folklore museum.

voyage.name: O Kafenes tou Kagiampi
voyage.content: Old fashioned tavern with traditional Greek dishes.

voyage.name: Kafeneio O Ntokos
voyage.content: Tiny place next to the fish market with delicious mezedes to accompany your beer or raki.

voyage.name: Kafeneio O Lakkos
voyage.content: Lost in a maze of small streets where different street artists have decorated the walls of the houses, Lakkos is particularly nice in the summer.

voyage.name: Pagopiion
voyage.content: (Ice-Factory)– A "quirky" restaurant and cafe/bar, at St Titus square, by the church. You can sit outside and enjoy the setting, or you might be tempted by the dramatic decor to sit inside. The food is excellent, and the menu different and interesting.

voyage.name: Ippokampos
voyage.content: Seafood and fish tavern by the sea side, popular with the locals.

voyage.name: Herbs' Garden
voyage.content: The name has been inspired from the traditional Cretan herbs. Offers a spectacular view of Heraklion's Venetian fortress and Cretan Sea. Opens from early afternoon and serves fresh fish and salads accompanied by local aperitifs and a variety of fine wines. Later in the afternoon there is special coffee and tea arrangements, fresh fruit juices, ice cream and cocktails.

voyage.name: Avli
voyage.content: Down an alleyway, in the cozied-up courtyard of a nondescript building. You know they are serious when the menu (and the sign) is in Greek only. Don't worry; the owner's daughter speaks perfect English and will sit down with you to explain the choices. A big selection of seasonal mezedhes and a smaller one of main dishes; all are super-fresh and most are local. No house wine; there's a board with today's by-the-glass

voyage.name: Epsilon Restaurant
voyage.address: roof garden Legacy Suites Hotel, Giorgou Anemogianni 43

voyage.name: Heraklion Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Read the online reviews before booking: fairly disgusting and not for the faint hearted.

voyage.name: Prince of Lillies Hotel
voyage.content: An excellent family-run hotel in Karteros, about 7 km east of Heraklion beyond the airport. (On bus route to Ag Nik with hourly buses.)

voyage.name: Mirabello Hotel
voyage.content: Good value, friendly atmosphere, very helpful staff. Rooms from €30-55 with discounts during low-season. Centrally located in a quiet part of the city. Nice views from the balcony.

voyage.name: Life Hotel
voyage.content: This hotel is walking distance to the port and very close to the bus station. Double €70. A good option if staying near the port and walking distance to the centre. It is also a 25-min walk from the airport and the directions are simple: Remain on Ikarou Ave until you see the hotel on the left. Staff are helpful and speak fluent English

voyage.name: Aquila Atlantis Hotel
voyage.content: Centrally located in a quiet area.

voyage.name: Candia Maris Resort - Adults Only
voyage.content: This 5-star spa resort is on the sandy beach of Amoudara, west of Heraklion. Tennis courts and 3 outdoor pools are featured amidst its 40,000-m² garden.

voyage.name: Lato Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: 4-star accommodation within a modern, friendly environment with panoramic views of the Venetian fortress.
